title: docs(idd-design-rationale): record that documenting a script's output contract must trace to the literal print/return statement, not infer from a type or variable name
body:
# docs(idd-design-rationale): record that documenting a script's output contract must trace to the literal print/return statement, not infer from a type or variable name

## Background

While drafting issue #2474's documentation of field-name variance
across this repository's evidence-collector helper scripts, an initial
draft made several confident, specific claims about which top-level
JSON keys a given helper actually returns. An independent
fact-checking critique pass found that roughly half of those claims
were wrong -- not because the underlying behavior was misunderstood,
but because a TypeScript **type name** or an internal **local
variable name** had been mistaken for an actual printed/returned
field. For example, `advisory-convergence.mts`'s printed object was
described as returning a `verdict` field: `verdict` is only the local
variable name holding the whole printed document
(`AdvisoryConvergenceVerdict`, the type), never a key nested inside
it. `discover-viability-gate.mts` was described as returning a
`passed` field: `passed` exists only on an internal per-issue helper
result, consumed to sort into the actually-printed
`viable`/`discarded` buckets, and is never copied into the printed
top-level object. A second, independent verification pass, re-tracing
every claim to the file's actual `JSON.stringify(...)` /
`process.stdout.write(...)` call site rather than to the nearest
plausible-looking name, caught and corrected every instance before the
documentation merged (`kurone-kito/idd-skill#2474`).

This is a distinct trap from an ordinary factual error: the wrong name
is often genuinely present in the same file, in a plausible-looking
spot (a type declaration, a locally-scoped intermediate variable), so
a skim-level read of the source can produce a confident,
specific-sounding claim that is still wrong. Nothing in the shared
work guidance currently names this trap or the concrete verification
habit that catches it.

## Proposed change

Add a dated entry under `docs/idd-design-rationale.md`'s (and its
canonical `idd-template/docs/idd-design-rationale.md` source's)
"## Documentation conventions" section, alongside the existing "Cite
the observed incident" convention, recording this pattern with
`kurone-kito/idd-skill#2474` cited per the established convention.
State the actionable takeaway plainly: when documenting what a script
or function actually returns or prints, trace every claimed field
name to its literal `JSON.stringify(...)` / `process.stdout.write(...)`
/ `return` call site in the current source -- never infer it from a
type name, an interface field, or a local variable name that merely
looks like it could be the same thing.

Do not edit `.github/instructions/idd-work.instructions.md` to add
this guidance directly: `bundle-work` sits at 94.51% utilization as of
2026-09-03, essentially no headroom before the 95% notice / 98%
hard-fail thresholds, and this same convention already routes
citation-bearing rationale to the budget-exempt
`docs/idd-design-rationale.md` instead.

Refs #1596 (non-blocking) -- names the pre-existing citation
convention this entry follows; already merged, informational only.

## Acceptance criteria

- A new, dated entry exists under `docs/idd-design-rationale.md`'s
  "## Documentation conventions" section (and its canonical
  `idd-template/docs/idd-design-rationale.md` source) citing
  `kurone-kito/idd-skill#2474`, following the established "cite the
  observed incident" convention.
- The entry states the actionable takeaway: trace a documented output
  field to its literal print/return call site in the current source,
  never to a type name, interface field, or local variable name
  alone.
- `node scripts/audit-docs.mjs --check` passes.
- `pnpm run docs:sync:check` passes (structure-mode pairs are not
  auto-checked for content; verify the canonical and generated copies
  stay consistent by hand).

## Candidate files

- `idd-template/docs/idd-design-rationale.md`
- `docs/idd-design-rationale.md`
